## 2. Variables

### A. Deservingness and Power consolidation

```{r, prisonerdeserves}

# pretty much done, maybe standardize later?

```

Standardize? No -- in my prelim, I write: To ensure that I do not control for a variable that is conceptually or empirically too close to the deservingness of incarcerated people when it is the dependent variable, I exclude any deservingness ratings for groups that are substantively overlapping or highly correlated. Including those could absorb variance in the outcome or introduce post-treatment bias by controlling for a related evaluative construct. I also avoid using global composite or average deservingness scores across all groups – for example, a respondent's mean deservingnesss rating across all 65 groups they evaluated – because that composite would include the rating of incarcerated people itself, introducing potential collinearity and making it difficult to isolate the unique effect of contact. This modeling strategy attempts to preserve interpretability and ensuring that the effect of policy contact is estimated with respect to unstandardized, target-specific deservingness scores. 12

12 While constructing composite or control variables involving other deservingness targets, I assess whether their inclusion introduces collinearity or conceptual overlap with the dependent variable. In particular, I examine correlations between group-level deservingness ratings to ensure that any included groups are not too closely tied to perceptions of incarcerated people. If preliminary checks reveal that including a particular group (e.g., “criminals” or “formerly incarcerated individuals”) would obscure key variance or conflate target constructs, I exclude it from the model and treat it as conceptually non-distinct for the purposes of this analysis.

### B. Experiences - Basic Coding

#### Impact Plus (Constructing For-Analysis)

```{r, impactvar}

#counting the *total* of those who said they were incarcerated, know incarcerated, or victims)

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    impact = if_else(
      q4_1_1 == 1 | q4_1_2 == 1 | q4_2_1 == 1,
      1, 0,
      missing = NA_real_
    )
  )

# post Aug 2026 version with casewhen,where  incarc = 0 to mean impact = 0 (no impact, not just no incarceration):

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    incarc = case_when(
      q4_1_1 == 1 ~ 1, 
      impact == 0 ~ 0, 
      TRUE ~ NA_real_ #"otherwise, assign NA"
    )
  )

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    knowincarc = case_when(
      q4_1_2 == 1 ~ 1, 
      impact == 0 ~ 0, 
      TRUE ~ NA_real_ #"otherwise, assign NA"
    )
  )

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    vict = case_when(
      q4_2_1 == 1 ~ 1, 
      impact == 0 ~ 0, 
      TRUE ~ NA_real_ #"otherwise, assign NA"
    )
  )

```

### G. Race

q51\_ ▢ White (1) ▢ Black or African American (2) ▢ Native American / Alaska Native (3) ▢ Asian / Asian American (4) ▢ Native Hawaiian / Other Pacific Islander (5) ▢ Middle Eastern/ North African (6) ▢ Hispanic/Latino/a/e (7) ▢ My preferred response not listed (8)

-measured as set of binary indicator variables in the survey, rather than as one categorical race variable. - 1 = selected that category - 0 = ? did not select? - NA = c

```{r}
#convert + clean
race_vars <- paste0("q51_", 1:8)

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(race_vars), ~ na_if(as.numeric(.x), -99)))

#rename
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  rename(
    white = q51_1,
    black = q51_2,
    hisp_latino = q51_7,
    asian_am = q51_4,
    native_am = q51_3,
    pac_island = q51_5,
    mena = q51_6,
    race_notlisted = q51_8
  )

race_vars <- c("white", "black", "hisp_latino", "asian_am",
               "native_am", "pac_island", "mena", "race_notlisted")
```

Responses -- noting consistent NAs so NAs are missing
```{r}
raw_data_cleaned %>%
  select(all_of(race_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "val") %>%
  count(var, val) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = val, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```


How many multiracial respondents?
```{r}
#row level counts
race_df <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    n_races   = rowSums(across(all_of(race_vars), ~ .x == 1), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_missing = rowSums(across(all_of(race_vars), is.na)),
    race_item_answered = n_races > 0,
    multiracial = case_when(
      !race_item_answered ~ NA,
      n_races >= 2        ~ TRUE,
      n_races == 1        ~ FALSE
    )
  )

count(race_df, n_races)
count(race_df, multiracial)
```


```{r}
# combinations
combo_counts <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(.id = row_number()) %>%
  select(.id, all_of(race_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-.id, names_to = "race", values_to = "selected") %>%
  filter(selected == 1) %>%                      # drops both 0s and NAs
  mutate(race = factor(race, levels = race_vars)) %>%
  arrange(.id, race) %>%
  group_by(.id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_races    = n(),
    race_combo = paste(race, collapse = " + "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  count(n_races, race_combo, name = "n") %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

combo_counts                                # everything
filter(combo_counts, n_races >= 2)          # multiracial combos only
```


```{r}
# pairs
race_mat <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  select(all_of(race_vars)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace_na(as.integer(.x == 1), 0L))) %>%
  as.matrix()

co_occur <- crossprod(race_mat)   # diagonal = marginal totals
co_occur
```

### H. Party + Ideology controls

```{r}

#raw_data_cleaned %>% count(q47)

#clean dem 101
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(dem101 = na_if(as.numeric(dem101), -99))

#party ID dummies
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    Republican = case_when(
      dem101 == 1 ~ 1,
      dem101 %in% c(2, 3, 4) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    Democrat = case_when(
      dem101 == 2 ~ 1,
      dem101 %in% c(1, 3, 4) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

#clean ideology
#ummary(raw_data_cleaned$q46)
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    q46 = na_if(as.numeric(q46), -99),
    q47 = na_if(as.numeric(q47), -99)
  )

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    fiscal_ideology = ifelse(!is.na(q46), 6 - q46, NA),#now 0 = very lib, 5 = very conservative (left to right)
    social_ideology = ifelse(!is.na(q47), 6 - q47, NA)
  )

#summary(raw_data_cleaned$fiscal_ideology)

table(raw_data_cleaned$politcs) # already coded so that left to right

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%

     )
```

### I. Gender

```{r, gender}
#raw_data_cleaned %>% count(q55)

#trans clean

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(q55 = na_if(as.numeric(q55), -99))

#trans indicator
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(trans_id = case_when(
    q55 == 1 ~ 1,
    q55 %in% c(2, 3) ~ 0,  # Conservative approach: counts only self-identified trans as 1
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ))


#gender clean
gender_vars <- paste0("q56_", 1:4)

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(gender_vars), ~ na_if(as.numeric(.x), -99)))


#constructing the gender binary
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(gender = case_when(
    q56_2 == 1 ~ 1,  # Selected man
    q56_1 == 1 & (q56_2 != 1 | is.na(q56_2)) ~ 0,  # Woman only or with genderqueer/other
    q56_3 == 1 | q56_4 == 1 ~ 0,  # Genderqueer or other, no man selected
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ))


```

### J. Victim Analysis Vars

```{r}

# police policies

# Originally 6 = strong oppose, 7= somewhat oppose, 8 = neutral, 9 = somewhat support, 10 = strong support

# Define Q25 police items
police_items <- c("q15_1", "q15_2", "q15_3", "q15_4", "q15_5")

# Step 1: Recode -99 to NA and ensure numeric
raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(police_items), ~ na_if(as.numeric(.), -99)))

# Step 2: Recode so 1-5 (6 = strong oppose → 1 = strong oppose, 
# 7 = somewhat oppose → 2 = somewhat oppose, 
# 8 = neutral → 3 = neutral, 
# 9 = somewhat support → 4 = somewhat support,
#10 = strong support → 5 = strong support)

raw_data_cleaned <- raw_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(police_items),
    ~ case_when(
    . == 6 ~ 1,          
    . == 7 ~ 2,
    . == 8 ~ 3,
    . == 9 ~ 4,
    . == 10 ~ 5,        
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),  
    .names = "{.col}_1_to_5"
  ))

police_items_1_to_5 <- c(
  "q15_1_1_to_5",
  "q15_2_1_to_5",
  "q15_3_1_to_5",
  "q15_4_1_to_5",
  "q15_5_1_to_5"
)

```

Note:

Approximately 561 respondents did not provide responses to the political behavior items (government attention, past vote, intended vote). Missingness is perfectly overlapping across these items, indicating that these questions were likely administered to a subset of respondents rather than reflecting item-level nonresponse.
